content:
When dispatching a subagent, the short description shown in the UI must END with the agent type in parentheses: `Verify the mirror (test)`, `Build the task dialog (frontend)`, `Review the depth guard (reviewer)`, `Survey the flusher (Explore)`.

WHY: that description is the ONLY thing the user sees while an agent runs in the background. Stated by the user on 2026-09-05: "when running agents in the background put names for them in the parantesis. some times i can not tell which agent type it is." A column of chips that all say "Investigating the failure" says nothing about which specialist is working, and the user cannot redirect a dispatch they cannot identify.

It costs nothing - three words in a field that is already required - so there is no case where skipping it is justified, including a single dispatch with no other agent running.

Written into the code as well as here, so it survives a session that never loads this rule: enforcement.agent_team_line() (the per-turn line) and agent_team_intro() (the session-start brief) both say it, and agents/pm.md carries it for a dispatched pm lead.
summary: When dispatching a subagent, the short description shown in the UI must END with the agent type in parentheses: `Verify...
title: Name the agent type in every dispatch description

content:
TWO HALVES, both from the same incident on 2026-09-04.

FOR THE AGENT: pass `project=` on every task and memory WRITE. Never rely on the resolved active project for a mutation. memory_task_plan was called without it, resolved to a different project than the session was working in, created seven tasks there, and auto-mirroring pushed them onto that project's asoode board within seconds. Cleanup meant archiving seven remote cards and deleting seven local rows. A read resolving loosely is a papercut; a WRITE resolving loosely puts data in the wrong project, which the "never cross-link projects" rule exists to prevent and cannot repair after the fact.

FOR THE CODE: the daemon's active project is a PROCESS GLOBAL shared by the daemon, every MCP session, every subagent and the management UI at once. The UI's project switcher used to call set_active_project(), so clicking a project in the panel silently redirected the writes of every running Claude session to it. Fixed: web/routes.py keeps the UI's selection under its own key (UI_ACTIVE_PROJECT_KEY), and only memory_use / memory_session_start - called by the client that owns the session - may set the MCP active project.

DO NOT re-wire the UI to the shared global for convenience, and do not add another reader-side surface that writes it. A viewer must never steer a writer. tests/test_active_project_isolation.py asserts the web routes cannot even reach set_active_project.

STILL OPEN, which is why the explicit-project half is not optional: the global is still ONE value for ALL MCP sessions. Two Claude sessions working different projects through the same daemon can still redirect each other, and subagents are MCP clients of that same daemon. Until it is per-caller, explicitness is the only real protection.
summary: TWO HALVES, both from the same incident on 2026-09-04
title: A write names its project explicitly; no viewer may steer a writer

content:
Every task gets a description that states the requirement in full: what is wanted, why, the constraint that shapes it, and the files or endpoints involved. A bare title is a reminder, not a requirement - it loses exactly the implementation detail the task list exists to preserve.

As work proceeds, comment on the task with what is learned: the decision taken and its alternative, the trap found, the thing that turned out to be wrong. A task should read back as a complete account of its own implementation. Anything that outlives the task still also goes to a rule/decision/architecture memory.
summary: Every task gets a description that states the requirement in full: what is wanted, why, the constraint that shapes it,...
title: A task must carry enough detail to be implemented without the conversation

content:
When a platform supports a field, USE IT - do not settle for the local copy. Time spent is the one that was missed repeatedly: memory_task_start/stop/done record time entries locally, and none of it reached asoode, so every task on the board read 0 minutes while the local store held real work. asoode has POST /tasks/:id/spend-time {begin, end}; the interface must expose time tracking as a capability and the flusher must mirror it like any other mutation.

The general rule: if the local store records something and the provider can represent it, mirroring it is part of the feature, not an enhancement. Check the platform's DTOs for what is representable before deciding what to send.
summary: When a platform supports a field, USE IT - do not settle for the local copy
title: Mirror everything the provider can hold, time tracking included

content:
DuckDB allows ONE writer per file across processes, and the launchd daemon holds that lock for every project it has opened. So any CLI command that writes to a project database must go through the daemon's HTTP API when one is reachable (memory_mcp/daemon_client.py: `run(path, method, payload, local)`), and open the file directly only when nothing answers on 127.0.0.1:<daemon_port>.

WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC: `memory-mcp asoode push` crashed at the FIRST local write, which happens AFTER the remote create. It made real tasks on the board and then died recording the mapping - remote rows the local store has no note of, the exact shape that produced 54 duplicate tasks once already. A write that does half its work and then reliably fails is a data bug, not a papercut.

Two rules that fall out of it, both load-bearing:
- A DaemonError (the daemon answered and refused) must NOT fall back to local. The request reached the process that owns the lock; retrying locally either fails the same way or fails on the lock and hides the real reason. Only DaemonUnavailable - nothing listening - is a reason to fall back.
- Adding a CLI write means checking there is an HTTP route for it. `import` had no route and had to be added; links/link/attach/push already did.

Reads that never touch a project DuckDB (`asoode boards`, which only uses the provider and the SQLite credential store) do not need routing - do not add ceremony where there is no lock to conflict with.
summary: DuckDB allows ONE writer per file across processes, and the launchd daemon holds that lock for every project it has...
title: A CLI write asks the daemon; it never opens a project database the daemon holds

content:
Whenever a full task is done and tested - the change complete, the suite green if code it covers changed, the test agent's live verification green - increment the version and push. Stated by the user on 2026-09-05: "whenever a full task is done and tested you shall increment the version and push."

How, in this repo: `./scripts/release.sh` (patch by default; `minor` for a feature-level change such as a new mirror path or a new agent; `major` for a breaking one). It bumps pyproject.toml, src/memory_mcp/__init__.py and uv.lock, commits "Release vX.Y.Z", tags vX.Y.Z and pushes both; the tag is what publishes the Docker image. The working tree must be clean and on main. The script runs the full suite by default: pass SKIP_TESTS=1 when the suite has already run on this exact code, or when nothing the suite covers changed (docs, agents, snapshot, a version bump) - the suite is evidence about code, not a ritual, and a four-minute release for a docs change is exactly what the user finds annoying. There is no pre-commit hook. Then `uv run memory-mcp-setup` so the daemon reports the new version.

Why it is a rule and not a habit: the installed daemon records its install commit and the update checker compares it against the branch tip, so an unversioned pile of commits is invisible as a release, and the version the daemon reports (memory_version, /api/health) stops meaning anything. One task, one version: the board's done task, the commit and the tag then tell the same story.
summary: Whenever a full task is done and tested - the change complete, the suite green if code it covers changed,...
title: A finished, tested task bumps the version and pushes

content:
Before a commit, the lead dispatches the `test` agent to verify the change that is about to be committed - against the RUNNING instance where the change is observable (the installed daemon, the UI, the bound board), not only the repo's own pytest suite. The commit waits for its report and happens only on a green one; a red report goes back to the implementing agent with the reproduction.

Stated by the user on 2026-09-05, correcting an earlier wording: "before the commit the test agent comes along and tests the work that has been done and is about to commit. The test suite is a set of tests you have for the mcp server code project, not its running instance."

The pytest suite is a different gate: it proves the code is internally consistent and runs once per finished change, by hand - there is no pre-commit hook (one was tried and removed the same day; a four-minute commit is not acceptable). The test agent proves the product still works - it exercises the daemon, the board and the browser like a person would, and reports what it actually saw. Both, in that order: suite first (seconds to minutes, catches your own mistakes), then the test agent (a dispatch, ~60k tokens, catches what the fixtures cannot), then the commit.

The brief to the test agent must say: what changed, where it is observable, the exact checks (create, change, read back), how to clean up what it creates, that it must run repo-side commands in the main checkout (its worktree is at the last commit), and that it must report failures with the actual output. Dispatch it in parallel with anything else that waits - a verification agent does not need to block the lead.
summary: Before a commit, the lead dispatches the `test` agent to verify the change that is about to be committed -...
title: The test agent verifies the work before it is committed

content:
A task description and a task comment are MARKDOWN, and must use the formatting: headings for the sections, bullet or numbered lists for the parts, **bold** for the thing that must not be missed, `code` for a symbol, a path or an endpoint, fenced blocks for output. A wall of unformatted prose is a choice now, not a constraint.

Stated by the user on 2026-09-05: "the task description and comment must support md or basic html support like list, etc... so use the proper formatting for description."

WHAT RENDERS IT: the local management UI renders markdown, and the asoode mirror converts to HTML on the way out (utils/richtext.py -> the asoode provider). asoode's own editor is TipTap, so the subset that survives a human editing the card is exactly p, h1-h3, ul/ol/li, blockquote, pre/code, hr, br, strong, em, s, code.

TWO THINGS THAT DO NOT SURVIVE, so do not reach for them:
- LINKS. `[text](url)` stays literal on purpose - StarterKit loads no Link extension and an anchor loses its URL the moment someone edits the card. Write the URL as plain text.
- TABLES. They degrade to a monospace code block. Readable, but a list is usually better.

Comments carry no headings: asoode's comment box is the same editor in compact mode, which has the heading node off, so `## X` is emitted as a bold paragraph. Use bold lead-ins and lists in a comment instead.
summary: A task description and a task comment are MARKDOWN, and must use the formatting: headings for the sections, bullet or...
title: Write task descriptions and comments as formatted markdown

content:
When this project is bound to an asoode work package, WORK ITS QUEUE - do not just report it.

The loop, one task at a time:
1. Read the bound board at session start. If tasks are waiting, take the highest-priority
   actionable one (state todo or in_progress). Do not ask which - pick and go.
2. Move it to in_progress on BOTH sides, and start time tracking.
3. Do the work. Record what comes up as it comes up: comments on the task, and anything
   that outlives it as a rule/decision/architecture memory.
4. Mark it done on both sides, stop the clock, then take the next one.

Do NOT auto-start a task whose state is blocked, blocker, paused, or cancelled, and stop to
ask when the work needs a decision only the user can make (an API choice, a product call, a
credential). Say which task you are on before starting it, so it can be redirected.

This deliberately OVERRIDES the default 'a queued task is a requirement, not an instruction'
contract for asoode-bound projects. That default still holds everywhere else: it protects the
capture case, where the user parks a requirement mid-session and does not want the session
derailed. Binding a project to an asoode board is the explicit opt-in to the loop.

SCOPE (added 2026-09-05, after a verification agent reported the conflict): this loop binds the
LEAD session - the one talking to the user. A dispatched agent works the task it was briefed
on and takes another only through memory_task_claim_next(session_id, role) when it is idle
and its brief allows it; a verification or review agent (test, reviewer) starts nothing on
the board, whatever the queue holds. A rule that made every subagent auto-claim work would
turn one dispatch into a swarm.
summary: When this project is bound to an asoode work package, WORK ITS QUEUE - do not just report it
title: Work the bound asoode task queue autonomously, one task at a time

content:
The full suite runs when actual code it covers has changed - src/memory_mcp/** or tests/** - once, when that change is complete. It does NOT run for a change that cannot affect it: docs, README, agents/*.md, the .claude-memory snapshot, hook scripts, a version bump, a frontend-only change (the frontend has its own build; `cd frontend && npm run build` is its check). Stated by the user on 2026-09-05: "the full suite test will run when actual code from where it covers gets changed; otherwise what is the benefit of checking something that did not have any effect - it is annoying."

Once, not once per file: a task that spans five files gets ONE run, when the change is complete, not after each file. While iterating, run the NARROW selection that covers what you are editing (pytest tests/test_x.py, or -k) - seconds, the fast feedback loop, what catches your own mistakes. The full suite answers a different question, did this break something elsewhere, and it takes about four minutes, so it is a deliberate step before installing and committing code, never a hook (the pre-commit hook was tried on 2026-09-05 and removed the same day). For a release, `SKIP_TESTS=1 ./scripts/release.sh` when the suite has just run on the same code or when nothing the suite covers changed.

Stated first by the user on 2026-09-04 after a task ran it three times over one piece of work. Same spirit as the standing constraint on token usage: be intelligent about cost, do not spend it re-confirming what has not changed.
summary: The full suite runs when actual code it covers has changed - src/memory_mcp/** or tests/** - once, when that change...
title: Run the full suite once per finished CODE change, and only when code it covers changed

content:
An implementation written from published API docs and tested only against a fake THIS codebase wrote is not a working integration. The tests prove the code is internally consistent; they cannot catch a wrong field name, a wrong query shape, a wrong auth header or a response that does not look like the docs - because the fake was written from the same misreading as the code.

Trello, Asana and Monday.com were written that way and deleted on 2026-09-04 for exactly this reason. asoode is the only real provider because it is the only one with a credential and a live server to verify against.

So: build the CONTRACT so providers can be added - interface, registry, conformance suite - but do not add a provider without credentials to verify it end to end. If asked for one anyway, say plainly that it will be unverified and what that means, rather than presenting a passing test suite as evidence it works.
summary: An implementation written from published API docs and tested only against a fake THIS codebase wrote is not a working...
title: Do not ship an integration that has never touched the live service

content:
Do not merge, rename away, delete or transfer tasks/memories between memory projects, and never link one project's boards to another. Project history is the asset this server exists to keep; mixing two projects corrupts both and is not recoverable from a snapshot, because the snapshot records the merged state as if it were true.

Duplicate registrations DO exist - the same repo registered twice under different slugs (see [[duplicate-memory-projects-in-this-workspace]]). The correct handling is to pick the project actually in use, act only on that one, and REPORT the duplicate for the user to retire. Never retire it yourself, and never 'tidy up' by consolidating.
summary: Do not merge, rename away, delete or transfer tasks/memories between memory projects, and never link one project's boards to another
title: Never merge, move or cross-link data between memory projects

content:
A task is the unit of work someone would pick up, review, or hand over. When part of one carries enough detail to be worked, argued about, or completed on its own, it should be a SUB-TASK (memory_task_add with parent_id, or memory_task_plan with parent_index) rather than a paragraph inside a description.

The test: could this part be assigned to someone else, or finished on a different day, without the parent being finished? Then it is a sub-task. Sub-tasks do not clutter the top-level list - it hides them the way a board does - so the cost of making one is near zero and the cost of burying real work in prose is that nobody sees it.

Still decompose by DELIVERABLE, not by step: 'write the test' is not a sub-task of 'add the endpoint', it is part of doing it.

TWO THINGS THE TOOLING NOW DOES, added 2026-09-05 after the user said "i have seen tasks with huge description, logically that much description usually requires couple of things to be fixed for":

1. EXACTLY ONE LEVEL. A task with a parent_id cannot take sub-tasks of its own; memory_task_add, memory_task_plan and the daemon's POST /tasks route all refuse it (TaskService._check_parentable). Not just a preference - asoode nests one level too, so a grandchild is a shape the board cannot hold. Promote first with memory_task_convert if a sub-task has really grown into a task.

2. A HINT, NOT A GATE. memory_task_add / _update / _plan return a `hint` when a top-level description is 1200+ characters AND carries three or more divisions (numbered items, checkboxes, headings). It is advisory: a long single explanation is a GOOD description and the hint deliberately stays quiet on one.

A SUB-TASK IS A FULL TASK: description, priority, labels, assignee, dates, estimate, role, comments and time tracking all work on it, and all of them mirror to the board. Do not downgrade a real deliverable to a checklist line because "it is only a sub-task".
summary: A task is the unit of work someone would pick up, review, or hand over
title: Decompose a task into sub-tasks when a part deserves its own record

content:
If a task has an attachment - a screenshot, a log, a diff, a generated report - it must reach the remote task's attachments, not just sit locally. asoode takes them at POST /tasks/:taskId/attach as multipart with the file field named `files` (tasks.controller.ts:280, FileInterceptor('files')), and has rename/remove/cover on /tasks/attachment/:id.

This is the same rule as time tracking, which had to be asked for repeatedly: if the local store holds something and the provider can represent it, mirroring it is part of the feature. Check the platform's endpoints for what is representable before deciding what to send. An attachment that exists only locally is invisible to everyone else looking at the board, which defeats the point of mirroring at all.
summary: If a task has an attachment - a screenshot, a log, a diff, a generated report - it must reach...
title: A task's attachments belong on the remote task too

content: After fixing any bug in this project, you must update the local installation so the running daemon reflects the fix. Rebuild the frontend if it changed (cd frontend && npm run build), then run `uv run memory-mcp-setup` to reinstall the runtime/UI and reload the launchd daemon, and verify the daemon is healthy. A bug fix is not considered complete until the local installation has been updated.
summary: After fixing any bug in this project, you must update the local installation so the running daemon reflects the fix
title: Update the local installation after every bug fix
